fact_check.claim: Cornell 2025-26 table: housing $13,744, food $7,604, books $1,234, personal $2,182, transportation 'Varies'
fact_check.note: All five lines match the 2025-26 table.

fact_check.claim: 2026-27 heading on the cost page has no figures
fact_check.note: 2026-27 section has headings and tabs but no figures.

fact_check.claim: Estimate leaves out premium on-campus or off-campus housing options
fact_check.note: Page says it excludes 'premium on-campus or off-campus housing options'.

fact_check.claim: Four priced lines total $24,764 a year
Housing $13,744 is divided by 12 ($1,145/mo) because off-campus leases usually run a full year; other lines over nine months
fact_check.note: $13,744 is exactly two semesters of the $6,872 dorm double, i.e. an academic-year (nine-month) figure. The finaid page does not say how many months the housing line covers. 'Off-campus leases usually run a full year' has no source. Dividing by 12 vs 9 changes the figure ($1,145 vs about $1,527) and is not explained against a source.

fact_check.claim: Off-campus page: look for housing that costs less for 12 months than the off-campus housing and dining budget; need calculated the same way on or off campus
fact_check.note: Both statements present.

fact_check.claim: Aid cannot cover security deposit, first and last month's rent, or rent in months you are not a registered student
fact_check.note: Page says aid can't pay upfront move-in costs such as deposit and first/last month's rent, nor rent for months not enrolled as a registered student.

fact_check.claim: Residence hall double is $6,872 per semester for 2026-27
fact_check.note: $6,872 per semester, $13,744 per year.

fact_check.claim: Dorm rate covers gas, electricity, garbage pickup and internet capped at 200 GB a month
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: A meal plan is required on top of the dorm rate
fact_check.note: The cited page does not say a meal plan is required, and no source link is given for the claim.

fact_check.claim: Collegetown houses run about $800 to $1,300 per person a month (the basis of the headline $1,500-$2,000 range and the rent row)
fact_check.note: The column does say $800-$1,300 per person (and says many houses are in poor condition). But the headline hard number rests only on one student columnist's opinion piece; it needs corroboration from current listings or an official/market source. Also the column gives higher-end apartments from about $1,450 (3-4 br) to $2,300 (studio), which the article omits and which pushes many students above the $2,000 top of the headline.

fact_check.claim: Mehring is a junior in ILR; lowest 2- or 3-bedroom apartment she saw was about $1,300; house rents roughly on par with on-campus housing
fact_check.note: Author is Class of 2027, ILR (a junior in fall 2025 is fine but she would be a senior now; 'a junior' should be dated or dropped). Other two statements match.

fact_check.claim: Column mentions unexpected costs for kitchen appliances and cleaning supplies, no prices
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: RentCafe Collegetown averages: studio $2,006, 1BR $2,342, 2BR $3,414, all rentals $2,815, down 2.59% from $2,890, updated October 30, 2026
fact_check.note: All figures and date match. (Page lists 3BR as not available.)

fact_check.claim: A $3,414 two-bedroom split two ways is $1,707 per person
fact_check.note: Arithmetic correct; labeled as ours.

fact_check.claim: 2022 Sun column by Niko Nguyen '22 describes roommates surprised that prices over $1,000 were per person, not per unit
fact_check.note: Column does say listed prices often reflect cost per person rather than per unit, but the fetch did not surface the 'roommates surprised' anecdote or the '$1,000' figure; verify wording or paraphrase only what the column says.

fact_check.claim: Nguyen signed his junior-year lease in October of his sophomore year
fact_check.note: Matches; students sign months or over a year ahead.

fact_check.claim: First-year students ride TCAT free with Cornell ID; after first year free after 6 p.m. weekdays and all day Saturday and Sunday
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: Cornell's page says to check myparking.cornell.edu for current pass pricing
fact_check.note: Page lists no prices and points to myparking.cornell.edu for discounted bus passes/OmniRide.

fact_check.claim: OmniRide pass costs $200 annually (bus pass row: $0 to about $17 a month)
fact_check.note: The $200 is from a November 2024 news article, not an official source, and is two years old; the article itself admits Cornell's page gives no price. Using it as a table figure needs an official current price. Also $200/12 = $17 conflicts with the nine-month division used for other lines ($200/9 = about $22).

fact_check.claim: CostLiving Ithaca: tight $2,190, moderate $3,650, comfortable $5,658 a month; 'CostLiving Engine, September 2026'
fact_check.note: Figures and data-source date match.

fact_check.claim: CostLiving says the tight tier works for students 'with university support or individuals with other income sources'
fact_check.note: That quoted phrase was not found in the fetched page text; verify or remove the quotation.

fact_check.claim: CostLiving says TCAT is free for students
fact_check.note: Page says 'Public transit (TCAT) is free for students but $1.50 per ride for others'.

fact_check.claim: Groceries about $2,960 a year, built on USDA food plan costs (internal guide)
fact_check.note: Figure lives in the internal guide /money/cornell-off-campus-meal-plan-or-cook-yourself-cost/ (file exists); no USDA link or figure appears in this article, and the article does not state which USDA plan or year. Link the USDA source here.

fact_check.claim: Phone, utilities and internet not priced; Cornell budget has no phone line
fact_check.note: Cost table has no phone line.

beats_top.query: cornell cost of living ithaca student monthly budget
beats_top.why: The top results are a law-school cost page and generic aggregators with inconsistent, undated estimates (about $2,100 to $4,400 a month); none builds an undergraduate monthly table from Cornell's own lines plus listings. Ours answers in the first paragraph, but the headline range excludes utilities and phone, which a student needs to budget, and relies on one columnist for rent.
changes: Add a clear utilities and phone line using sourced figures (or a sourced range, e.g. NYSEG/ISP/carrier published prices) so the total is a real monthly number, or show a second 'with utilities' total.
Corroborate the rent range with current listings or an official source and mention Mehring's $1,450-$2,300 higher-end apartment prices so the range is not understated.
Fix the month-divisor logic (9 vs 12) and use an official current bus-pass price.

fixes: Housing divisor: state that Cornell's $13,744 housing line equals two semesters of the $6,872 residence hall double (source https://scl.cornell.edu/residential-life/housing/housing-details/rates-amenities-licenses/housing-rates), so it is an academic-year figure; either show both $1,145 (over 12) and $1,527 (over 9) with a plain explanation, or drop the unsourced claim that 'off-campus leases usually run a full year' and cite https://finaid.cornell.edu/special-circumstances/living-campus for the 12-month comparison only.
Remove 'A meal plan is required on top' from the residence hall paragraph, or cite a Cornell dining/housing page that says it; the housing rates page does not.

The headline rent range ($800 to $1,300) rests only on a student columnist. Add at least one current non-opinion source (a current Collegetown listing page or the RentCafe data you already cite) for per-room rent, and add that the same column puts higher-end apartments at about $1,450 for a 3-4 bedroom up to $2,300 for a studio, link https://www.cornellsun.com/article/2025/09/maia-on-the-mic-the-collegetown-housing-hustle. Reconcile the headline range and the 'Total' row with that.

Replace the bus-pass $200 figure with the current price from https://myparking.cornell.edu (the page Cornell points to) and cite it; if it cannot be loaded, keep the Sun figure only in prose labeled 'reported in November 2024', not in the table. Use the same month divisor as the other lines ($200/9 = about $22, not $17).

Add a utilities and phone estimate or at least a sourced range (e.g. cite published NYSEG residential rates, a named provider's internet plan price, and a carrier plan price with URLs); the article currently gives no figure for them, so the monthly total is incomplete for a reader who needs a monthly budget. Show a 'with utilities' total.
Link the USDA food plan source (name the plan and year, with its URL) next to the $2,960 grocery figure instead of relying on the internal guide alone.

Remove or verify the CostLiving quotation 'with university support or individuals with other income sources'; it was not found on https://costliving.net/ithaca/. Paraphrase only what the page says (tight tier assumes shared housing and minimal dining out).

Nguyen column: paraphrase only what https://cornellsun.com/2022/08/04/nguyen-the-tale-of-cornells-broken-housing-market/ says (listed prices often reflect cost per person rather than per unit); remove 'roommates who were surprised that prices over $1,000 were per person' unless you can quote its location in the column.
Change 'Maia Mehring, a junior in the School of Industrial and Labor Relations' to 'a Cornell Daily Sun columnist (ILR, Class of 2027)', since the column is dated September 2025.
